mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the past month signals an improving labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past two months indicates a strong supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% over the same period, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it suggests a stable economic environment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals a strong economic growth, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
